ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: Figure 32(a) on the left side of the attached figure is a comparator circuit; the upper input of the operational amplifier is marked “−” and is connected to the input voltage ui; the lower input is marked “+” and is connected to the voltage-dividing node formed by R2 and R1. In the figure, R1 is connected from this node to ground, and R2 is connected from this node to the node on the right stabilized by the voltage regulator diode VD2, and this node is labeled +U2 = +6 V. Reasoning: At the comparator switching threshold, the input ui is equal to the non-inverting terminal reference voltage V+. The ideal operational amplifier input current is zero, so the R2-R1 voltage division is not affected by the input terminal, V+ = U2 * R1 / (R1 + R2). Substituting U2 = 6 V, R1 = 40 kΩ, R2 = 20 kΩ, gives UT1 = 6 * 40 / (40 + 20) = 4.0 V.

method.method_draft: First inspect the image to classify the circuit as an inverting Schmitt comparator with positive feedback to the non-inverting input. Use the textbook threshold expression UT1 = [R1/(R1+R2)]·UOH. From the text, take UOH as the Zener stable voltage U2=6 V and use R1=40 kΩ, R2=20 kΩ. Compute UT1=(40/60)·6=4.0 V.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: In figure 32(a), the comparator has the input ui applied to the inverting “−” terminal. The non-inverting “+” terminal is connected to a feedback divider: R2 from the output side back to the “+” input node, and R1 from that node to ground. The output is limited by the Zener diode network VD2, with the positive stable level indicated as +U2 = +6 V. This matches an inverting Schmitt comparator with positive feedback to the non-inverting input.

Reasoning: For this circuit, the assigned threshold expression is UT1 = [R1/(R1 + R2)]·UOH. The output high level UOH is set by the Zener stable voltage, so UOH = U2 = 6 V. With R1 = 40 kΩ and R2 = 20 kΩ, UT1 = [40/(40 + 20)] × 6 = (40/60) × 6 = 4.0 V.
